The 3D space two objects share

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/intersect.R
intersect_3d.Rd

intersect_3d() returns the part of space that is inside both x and y. It answers the question "what do these two share?". To ask only "do they share anything?", use intersects_3d(). To keep one object's values where the other is present, use mask().

Usage

intersect_3d(x, y, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatEnvelope,SpatEnvelope'
intersect_3d(x, y, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatVoxel,SpatVoxel'
intersect_3d(x, y)

# S4 method for class 'SpatEnvelope,SpatVoxel'
intersect_3d(x, y, bounds = c("midpoint", "top"), ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatVoxel,SpatEnvelope'
intersect_3d(x, y, bounds = c("midpoint", "top"), ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatEnvelope,ANY'
intersect_3d(x, y, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatVoxel,ANY'
intersect_3d(x, y)

# S4 method for class 'ANY,ANY'
intersect_3d(x, y, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatVector3D,SpatEnvelope'
intersect_3d(x, y, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatVector3D,SpatVoxel'
intersect_3d(x, y, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatEnvelope,SpatVector3D'
intersect_3d(x, y, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatVoxel,SpatVector3D'
intersect_3d(x, y, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatVector3D,SpatVector3D'
intersect_3d(x, y, ...)

Arguments

x, y

The two objects: two of SpatEnvelope, SpatVoxel and SpatVector3D polygons or points, in any pairing except two sets of points, or an envelope or voxel with a 2D object (a single-layer SpatRaster footprint or 2D polygons: SpatVector, sf, sfc). Rasters must share one grid (CRS, extent, resolution). netCDF files aren't accepted; load them with terra and wrap them with as_voxel() first.

...

Arguments for the voxel methods. They are an error when both inputs are envelopes, or when one is points and the other an envelope or a voxel.

bounds

Only when one input is a voxel and the other an envelope or SpatVector3D polygons. How the envelope or polygons are placed on the voxel's depth levels: "midpoint" (default) or "top". See envelope_to_voxel(). Not used when the voxel carries its own depth edges (see SpatVoxel). To measure the result, pass the same bounds to volume().

Value

SpatVector3D polygons when both inputs are polygons, and SpatVector3D points when one is points and the other polygons. A SpatEnvelope when both inputs are envelopes, or when one is an envelope and the other is 2D or a SpatVector3D. Otherwise a SpatVoxel of presence. Either is on the grid of the 3D input.

Details

At least one of x and y must be a 3D object: a SpatEnvelope, a SpatVoxel or SpatVector3D polygons or points. The other can be a 3D object too, or, with an envelope or voxel, a 2D object. A 2D object restricts the result horizontally and leaves its depths alone.

Two envelopes

Cell by cell, the result runs from the deeper depth_min to the shallower depth_max. Intervals that only touch share no water, so that cell is empty (NA).

Two voxels

Both must be sampled at the same depth levels. A level is in the result where both voxels occupy it.

An envelope and a voxel

The envelope is first placed on the voxel's depth levels with envelope_to_voxel(). The result is a voxel.

An envelope or voxel and a SpatRaster

The raster is a footprint. Its non-NA cells are inside; its values are not read. It must have one layer and be on the same grid.

An envelope or voxel and 2D polygons

A SpatVector, sf or sfc object. The polygons are rasterised onto the 3D object's grid. A cell is inside when a polygon touches it. Polygons in another CRS are projected first.

An envelope and SpatVector3D polygons

The polygons are first put on the envelope's grid with vector3d_to_envelope(), then compared as an envelope. Each cell a polygon touches gets its depth range; where polygons overlap, a cell gets the shallowest top and the deepest bottom, so a depth gap between two polygons over one cell is filled.

A voxel and SpatVector3D polygons

The polygons are first put on the voxel's grid and depth levels with vector3d_to_voxel(), one level at a time, then compared as a voxel. A depth gap between two polygons over one cell stays empty. When the voxel has no depth edges, you set each level's slab with bounds, as in envelope_to_voxel().

An envelope or voxel and SpatVector3D polygons, either way

The polygons' time intervals are dropped, with a message. Polygons that miss the grid, or a set with no polygons, give an empty result.

A voxel and SpatVector3D points

A point covers one cell and one depth level: the cell that holds it and the level whose depth is nearest the point's depth (a tie goes to the shallower level, as in extract_to_point()). The level is chosen by depth alone, so a point whose nearest level has no value in the voxel shares nothing there. When the voxel's depth edges give uneven slabs, the slab that contains a point can belong to another level; the nearest level is used. The result is a presence voxel on the voxel's levels, and bounds doesn't apply. Points off the grid share nothing. Points' times aren't compared, since a voxel shows one time step.

An envelope and SpatVector3D points

In each cell where a point's depth lies within the envelope's interval (both ends included), the result holds an interval from the shallowest such point to the deepest. A lone point gives a zero-thickness interval, so the result's volume() is 0: points have no volume.

SpatVector3D points and polygons

A point is inside a polygon when sf::st_intersects() finds its position in the outline (on WGS84 coordinates sf uses the sphere by default, where a point exactly on an edge may not count), its depth is within depth_min to depth_max and its time within the polygon's time interval. Depth and time include both ends (with dates, the interval covers all of its end day). A point or polygon without a time matches any time; one side with dates and the other with hours is an error. Each matching pair gives one point, numbered, with columns feature_id_x and feature_id_y naming the pair and the inputs' other columns dropped. Two sets of points share no space, so they are an error. Lines aren't supported; buffer_3d() turns them into polygons.

Two sets of SpatVector3D polygons

Each pair of polygons, one from x and one from y, whose outlines, depth ranges and times overlap gives one polygon: the shared outline (as sf::st_intersection()), the shared depth range, and the shared time interval. Depth ranges that only touch share no water. Time intervals include both ends, so with dates, two that share a day overlap on it, and with hours, two that meet at one instant overlap at that instant (so a polygon at a single time can meet another). A polygon without a time overlaps any time and passes on the other's interval. One set can't have dates while the other has hours. The result's feature IDs are numbers; columns feature_id_x and feature_id_y say which polygons each came from, and the inputs' other columns are dropped. Pairs that share nothing give no polygon, so the result can have none. To measure the overlap, use volume(intersect_3d(x, y)).

The order of x and y does not matter.

The result is a domain, not a field. An envelope result carries the shared depth interval. A voxel result carries presence: 1 where a level is shared, NA elsewhere, in layers named presence_depth=<value>. The cell values of a voxel input are not carried over. To keep them, use mask().

terra's intersect()

terra::intersect() on two rasters is a 2D test that ignores depth. On a SpatEnvelope or a SpatVoxel, in either position, it is an error that points to intersects_3d() and intersect_3d(). Plain rasters, vectors and extents keep terra's behaviour.

See also

intersects_3d() for the yes/no form; mask() to keep a voxel's values inside a domain; volume() for the volume of the result, in total or per cell. When one input is a voxel, the envelope is placed on its levels, so compare the overlap with volume(envelope_to_voxel(...)) rather than with the envelope's own volume.

Examples

fp <- terra::rast(nrows = 1, ncols = 3, xmin = 0, xmax = 3000,
                  ymin = 0, ymax = 1000,
                  crs = "+proj=laea +lat_0=0 +lon_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m")
terra::values(fp) <- c(1, 1, 1)

# Two species: one at 0-100 m, one at 50-200 m everywhere.
a <- as_envelope(fp, depth_min = 0, depth_max = 100)
b <- as_envelope(fp, depth_min = 50, depth_max = 200)

# They share 50-100 m in every cell.
shared <- intersect_3d(a, b)
terra::values(shared)
#>      depth_min depth_max
#> [1,]        50       100
#> [2,]        50       100
#> [3,]        50       100
volume(shared)
#> [1] 0.15

# With a voxel, the result is a presence voxel on the voxel's levels.
bv <- envelope_to_voxel(b, depths = c(0, 50, 100, 150, 200))
names(intersect_3d(a, bv))
#> [1] "presence_depth=0"   "presence_depth=50"  "presence_depth=100"
#> [4] "presence_depth=150" "presence_depth=200"

# With polygons, the envelope is kept where the polygon is.
poly <- terra::vect("POLYGON ((0 0, 2000 0, 2000 1000, 0 1000, 0 0))",
                    crs = terra::crs(fp))
terra::values(intersect_3d(a, poly))
#>      depth_min depth_max
#> [1,]         0       100
#> [2,]         0       100
#> [3,]        NA        NA

# With SpatVector3D polygons, the depth ranges are compared too: a polygon
# from 80 to 300 m over the first two cells shares 80-100 m with `a`.
deep <- as_vector3d(
  sf::st_sf(geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(
    "POLYGON ((0 0, 2000 0, 2000 1000, 0 1000, 0 0))",
    crs = terra::crs(fp)
  )),
  depth_min = 80, depth_max = 300
)
terra::values(intersect_3d(a, deep))
#>      depth_min depth_max
#> [1,]        80       100
#> [2,]        80       100
#> [3,]        NA        NA

# A SpatVector3D point covers the cell that holds it and, on a voxel, the
# level nearest its depth: here the 50 m level of `bv` in the first cell
# (the point is projected onto the grid's CRS).
detection <- as_vector3d(data.frame(lon = 0.0045, lat = 0.0045, depth = 60))
terra::values(intersect_3d(detection, bv))
#>      presence_depth=0 presence_depth=50 presence_depth=100 presence_depth=150
#> [1,]               NA                 1                 NA                 NA
#> [2,]               NA                NA                 NA                 NA
#> [3,]               NA                NA                 NA                 NA
#>      presence_depth=200
#> [1,]                 NA
#> [2,]                 NA
#> [3,]                 NA

# Two sets of SpatVector3D polygons give the polygons they share.
square <- function(x0) {
  sf::st_polygon(list(rbind(c(x0, 0), c(x0 + 2, 0), c(x0 + 2, 2),
                            c(x0, 2), c(x0, 0))))
}
mpa <- as_vector3d(
  sf::st_sf(geometry = sf::st_sfc(square(150), crs = 4326)),
  depth_min = 0, depth_max = 200
)
habitat <- as_vector3d(
  sf::st_sf(geometry = sf::st_sfc(square(151), crs = 4326)),
  depth_min = 100, depth_max = 500
)
shared <- intersect_3d(mpa, habitat)
as.data.frame(shared)[c("feature_id_x", "feature_id_y", "depth_min",
                        "depth_max")]
#>   feature_id_x feature_id_y depth_min depth_max
#> 1            1            1       100       200
volume(shared)
#> [1] 2461.484
